# Vertice & GrowthBook | First Meeting
Date: 2026-09-29 | Duration: 22.6299991607666m

## Summary
The client is a large Australian online furniture retailer with about 300 employees, warehouses in Melbourne, and markets in Australia and New Zealand. It has used Optimizely for two years but is evaluating whether it remains the best fit, with interest in simpler solutions offering better margins. GrowthBook was presented as strong in experimentation, feature flagging, and A/B testing, while Optimizely was described as more marketing-focused. Integration with Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, BigQuery, Google Analytics, Amplitude, Mixpanel, and Segment is important. GrowthBook’s pricing includes a transparent base platform fee and per-user seats, with no traffic or event charges. The client has reduced its vendor shortlist from five to two and will use an RFP, demo/Q&A, and commercial negotiation process. A pilot is likely, potentially involving a six-month contract followed by an extension, while strategic contracts typically last one to three years. A decision is expected before year-end, with the pilot starting after the Christmas peak. David Court will provide requirements and application insights, Marcel Geldner will send follow-up materials, and a GrowthBook solution engineer is expected to join the next meeting, likely in October.

## Keywords
Optimizely, GrowthBook, experimentation, feature flagging, pricing model, APAC expansion

## Action Items
**David Court**  
Coordinate next client meeting for October (16:44)  
Send client requirements and dates to Marcel Geldner (20:01)  

**Marcel Geldner**  
Arrange GrowthBook solution engineer involvement (17:16)  
Send presentation slides to client (20:01)  
Prepare meeting summary and follow-up questions (20:01)

# Vertice & GrowthBook | Introduction Call and Evaluation
Date: 2026-10-20 | Duration: 46.810001373291016m

## Summary
Optimizely’s three-year contract is nearing its end, prompting a reassessment of vendors as business needs evolve and AI scales internal capabilities. Product teams currently lead web and feature experimentation, with engineering involved in backend changes, while Flutter supports mobile A/B testing and shared variant logic. BigQuery consolidates Snowplow, Optimizely, and other tracking data, but a seven-percent discrepancy remains unresolved. Tracking is also fragmented because blockers suppress events, page changes lose requests, and multiple trackers can collide; reverse-proxy routing through Cloudflare improved receipt-page tracking. The technical environment is transitioning from a PHP frontend and backend toward Node.js, with Microsoft SQL Server and added coordination challenges. GrowthBook can query BigQuery, reuse the Snowplow pipeline, allocate traffic through SDKs, support feature flags, product analytics, visual editing, and cloud or self-hosted deployment. Evaluation activities, including documentation, workshops, testing, case studies, and customer references, are planned through February.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Optimizely migration, Experimentation platform, BigQuery warehouse, Feature flags, A/B testing
